the proposed multi-objective MPC is a promising control technique for the PUC topology, as it achieves high accuracy in grid current injection, and it is capable of balancing the capacitors voltage, which is a critical issue for this topology.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1) the design of the MPC for the PUC topology with the objective of controlling the current, the PF and the capacitor voltages; 2) the implementation and validation of the designed MPC on the experimental platform.
the following aspects: 1) A multi-objective cost function is defined and optimized for the MPC, which leads to a flexible and easy tuning of the MPC.

the following contributions: (i) the design of a multi-objective MPC for 15-level PUC inverter, (ii) the use of a novel cost function that includes the capacitors' voltage balancing term in the MPC optimization, (iii) the use of the pre-charge circuits in case of using a PI current controller, (iv) the use of MPC for the pre-charge control in case of using MPC for the grid current control.

the proposed MPC is an attractive solution for the presented PUC grid-tied inverter.

the proposed MPC can be used as a single solution for the grid current and capacitor voltage control in the PUC topology.
the proposed MPC is a flexible and efficient solution for grid-tied PUC inverter, which is able to achieve high power quality with minimum number of control variables.
the proposed MPC achieves the best trade-off for the considered objectives, which is not the case when using traditional PI controllers.
